encounters.cc: Persistent throat discomfort and changes in voice following anterior neck surgery

lines: Persistent throat discomfort and changes in voice following anterior neck surgery

The 55-year-old male with colorectal cancer s/p resection, urethral stricture, diverticulosis, and pancreatitis, last seen in Urology on 2020-01-15, returns with voice changes that began shortly after anterior neck surgery.
Since the procedure, he reports difficulty reaching high-pitched tones when speaking and experiences mild choking when attempting to swallow liquids.
He denies hoarseness, aspiration of solids, or shortness of breath.
- Urethral stricture secondary to traumatic pelvic fracture

He underwent the operation two months ago to address a multinodular thyroid enlargement that was causing mild dysphagia.
Smoking: Former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 3 years ago.
Physical examination reveals a well-healed anterior cervical scar and symmetric elevation of the palate.
His speech is clear but notably weak and breathy during attempts to project his voice.
Flexible laryngoscopy shows normal vocal cord motion but poor tensioning of the ipsilateral vocal fold during phonation.
Sensation above the vocal cords is diminished on the affected side.

encounters.cc: Admitted to the intensive care unit following a motor vehicle collision with multiple head injuries

lines: Admitted to the intensive care unit following a motor vehicle collision with multiple head injuries
The patient is a 56-year-old male with urethral stricture and colorectal adenocarcinoma admitted after trauma.
He has been intubated and mechanically ventilated.
He is currently being hyperventilated to reduce intracranial pressure.
Despite this, his intracranial hypertension persists, and the medical team decides to initiate pharmacologic therapy.

encounters.cc: Admitted after near-drowning incident with progressive dyspnea and refractory hypoxemia

lines: Admitted after near-drowning incident with progressive dyspnea and refractory hypoxemia
He is a 58-year-old male with history of colorectal adenocarcinoma, urethral stricture, and prior ARDS presenting following a near-drowning incident.
He was intubated at the scene and placed on mechanical ventilation with a high inspired oxygen fraction (FiO₂ 1.0) to correct severe hypoxemia.
During the following 72 hours, his oxygenation initially improves, but he later develops progressive dyspnea and diffuse rales.

lines: Oxygen saturation gradually decreasing over several hours despite stable ventilator settings following emergency abdominal surgery
This 59-year-old with history of colorectal resection, prior ARDS from pancreatitis, and traumatic pelvic fracture presents to ICU following emergency abdominal surgery for perforated diverticulitis.
He is intubated and mechanically ventilated in the ICU.
He has been sedated and stable on ventilator for past 2 days.
He remains afebrile, hemodynamically stable, and has no signs of infection.
